result.title: Partially Observable Zero-shot coordination by Predicting Intention of Partner
result.summary: Zero-shot coordination in embodied settings requires acting while the partner is intermittently out of view, leaving existing methods with ambiguous partner representations and uncertainty over hidden partner states. We propose Predicting Intention of Partner (PIP) to jointly address these challenges. PIP uses a Joint-view VAE to distill richer training-time evidence from the union of both agents' local observations into a partner representation available from local observations alone. Partner-state Belief networks further infer the partner's hidden location and behavioral tendencies from the ego agent's interaction history. We evaluate PIP in Burrito-PO, Overcooked-PO, and a Melting Pot substrate, together with a human evaluation in Burrito-PO. PIP attains the highest mean performance among the compared methods across all three benchmarks. Human evaluation and diagnostic analyses further support coordination with unseen partners and the contributions of both components under partner occlusion.

AI.brief_summary: PIP 研究具身场景下伙伴间歇不可见时的零样本协作：用 Joint-view VAE 把双方局部观测的联合信息蒸馏成仅凭本地观测即可获得的伙伴表征，并用伙伴状态信念网络从交互历史推断伙伴的隐藏位置与行为倾向，在三个基准与人类评测中取得最高平均表现。
AI.relevance_reason: 其信念状态推断与「从局部证据蒸馏伙伴表征」的思路，可能可供核查 LVR 中在不完整观测下维护内部状态、用信念指导取证据与停止决策的类比，但对象是合作者而非视觉 latent，联系需较多验证。
